questions.title: The metaphase checkpoint verifies spindle attachment
questions.subject: fnd
questions.question: Which specific cell cycle checkpoint verifies proper spindle attachment to the chromosomes before allowing the cell to proceed?

explanations.A: Incorrect. The G1 checkpoint verifies that the cell has adequate size, nutrients and an intact genome before committing to DNA replication; it does not monitor spindle attachment, which has not yet occurred at that stage.
explanations.B: Correct. The metaphase (spindle-assembly) checkpoint monitors whether every chromosome's kinetochore is correctly attached to spindle microtubules from opposite poles, and it blocks entry into anaphase until every chromosome is properly bi-oriented, preventing chromosome missegregation. Only once every chromosome is correctly bi-oriented does the checkpoint release its block, allowing sister chromatids to separate at anaphase.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The G2 checkpoint verifies that DNA replication is complete and undamaged before the cell enters mitosis; spindle attachment has not yet been established at that stage either.
explanations.D: Incorrect. There is no dedicated 'S phase checkpoint' monitoring spindle attachment; DNA-damage surveillance during S phase is a separate mechanism from the metaphase checkpoint's spindle-attachment role.

questions.learning_objective: State that the metaphase (spindle-assembly) checkpoint verifies correct attachment of every chromosome's kinetochore to the mitotic spindle before allowing the cell to proceed into anaphase.
